issues.description: The solution defines the pixel-writing subroutine with the label '.set_pixel' (leading dot), while the template and problem statement refer to the subroutine as 'set_pixel' and call 'call set_pixel' from main. This name mismatch (leading dot in the solution label) is a structural inconsistency that can prevent the call from resolving correctly and will confuse students about the required symbol name and linkage.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent symbol name for the subroutine across template and solution. Rename the solution label from '.set_pixel' to 'set_pixel' (or change the call sites to 'call .set_pixel') so the label and the call match. Ensure the label is declared global if needed and that symbol naming follows the assembler conventions used in the template.

issues.description: The procedure name used for the same conceptual entity 'set_pixel' is inconsistent: the problem statement and the template define/reference the routine as set_pixel, but the solution defines the routine as .set_pixel (leading dot). This mismatch can confuse students when mapping the problem description and the template to the provided solution code and when searching for the implementation to compare against the TODO.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the routine name identical across artifacts. Rename the solution label from .set_pixel to set_pixel (or update the calls to call .set_pixel in both template and problem references), so the problem statement, template, and solution consistently use the same identifier.
